clips.send: Honeybees do one of the most important jobs on Earth: they help grow our food. As a bee drinks nectar, pollen sticks to its fuzzy body and rubs off on the next flower. That moved pollen lets plants make fruit and seeds. Apples, almonds, blueberries and many other crops depend on bee visits. Inside the hive, a single queen can lay more than 1,500 eggs a day. Young workers clean cells and feed larvae, older ones build wax and guard the door, and the oldest fly out to gather food. A honeybee colony works like a well-organized city, with every bee doing a job. Honeybees also share information in an amazing way. A forager that finds flowers does a “waggle dance” that shows other bees the direction and distance to the food. Scientist Karl von Frisch decoded the dance and won a Nobel Prize in 1973. A bee’s wings beat more than 200 times a second. Beekeepers have noticed something worrying. Honeybee colonies today face serious threats. Tiny parasites called varroa mites, pesticides, diseases and a shortage of wildflowers all weaken colonies. In some recent years, US beekeepers have reported losing a third or more of their hives. Farmers are planting strips of wildflowers, and scientists are breeding bees that resist mites. Protecting honeybees means protecting the food on our tables.

clips.send: 蜜蜂做着地球上最重要的工作之一：帮助我们种出粮食。 蜜蜂吸花蜜时，花粉粘在它毛茸茸的身上，又蹭到下一朵花上。 被带走的花粉让植物结出果实和种子。 苹果、杏仁、蓝莓和许多其他作物都离不开蜜蜂的造访。 蜂巢里，一只蜂王一天能产下 1500 多枚卵。 年轻的工蜂清洁巢房、喂养幼虫，年长一些的筑蜡、守门，最年长的飞出去采集食物。 一个蜂群就像一座井井有条的城市，每只蜜蜂都有自己的工作。 蜜蜂还用一种神奇的方式交流信息。 找到花的采集蜂会跳“摇摆舞”，告诉同伴食物的方向和距离。 科学家卡尔·冯·弗里希破解了这种舞蹈，并于 1973 年获得诺贝尔奖。 蜜蜂的翅膀每秒扇动 200 多次。 养蜂人注意到了一件令人担忧的事。 如今，蜂群正面临严重的威胁。 叫作瓦螨的微小寄生虫、农药、疾病和野花减少，都在削弱蜂群。 近些年里，有些年份美国养蜂人报告损失了三分之一甚至更多的蜂箱。 农民在田边种上一条条野花带，科学家在培育能抵抗螨虫的蜜蜂。 保护蜜蜂，就是保护我们餐桌上的食物。
